methodology_notes: Province focus: Neuquén (Vaca Muerta hub) plus Río Negro, Mendoza, San Juan, Salta, Catamarca, Chubut, Santa Cruz — selected where SIPA registered employment and/or energy/mining production show sustained outperformance vs national averages in the fetch window.

Affordability net wage: gross OEDE/SIPA provincial average total remuneration (May 2026 for comparisons; June/December include SAC) minus employee social security (17%: 11% jubilación + 3% PAMI + 3% obra social) minus estimated Ganancias (fourth-category monthly scale for 2026 — approximation from AFIP published brackets; not individualized).
National CPI month-on-month KPI uses INDEC 145.3_INGNACUAL_DICI_M_38 (decimal rate ×100 for display).
Patagonia provinces (Neuquén, Río Negro, Chubut, Santa Cruz): additional 22% deduction on taxable income for Ganancias (zona patagónica) applied before tax calculation.
Single-adult food & basics cost proxy: regional Canasta Básica Total (INDEC) × 0.55 — equivalence factor labeled estimate (official CBT is a reference household basket).
Household cost proxy: regional CBT at published INDEC family-basket level (no equivalence scaling).
GBA cost benchmark uses Pampeana regional canasta series where no dedicated GBA CBT series exists in datos.gob.ar (documented caveat).
Rent inputs: published market survey figures below; not from a machine-readable Zonaprop/Argenprop API.

selection_rationale: Growing provinces in this dashboard combine (i) positive multi-year SIPA private registered job growth and (ii) energy/mining or export momentum — Neuquén and Chubut via hydrocarbon basins, Mendoza/San Juan via mining & industry, Salta/Catamarca via mining & services, Santa Cruz via oil & logistics.
